eyebrow: Freedom Reads · Washington State Penitentiary, ILP 2026 Tour · 11 Jun 2026 · Rapid-fire book reviews
title: The ILP 2026 books:
title_short: ILP books · A Small Piece of Yourself
headline: Four Inside Literary Prize books in one breath, reviewed by a reader inside.
story: A judge inside Washington State Penitentiary gives each book one sharp line: Martyr!, My Friends, The Book Censor's Library and All Fours. Fast cuts, one title card per book.

Then the turn: “you will find a small piece of yourself in every single one of the books.” This video sells the reading list to book lovers. It is not about his life or about prison. The judge is Brandon, the same man as the “Reading Was an Escape” cut.
do: Frame 1 is the judge speaking about Martyr!, with the word <q>Martyr!</q> on screen. No title card at 0:00.
One type-only book card per title, from 0:02 on. Titles exactly as printed on the books.
Cut fast between books. Cover each jump with library B-roll.
Hold on him for the last line. Music out under it.
Card “Brandon · ILP 2026 judge” at 0:09, after the hook.
dont: No title card, logo or fade at 0:00.
No life story or prison talk. This one is about the books.
No made-up book covers. Use real cover art only if Nick supplies it.
Don't use his “A9” review (Ædnan). It is not in this cut.

checklist: “Freedom Reads” is two words with two r's. Never “FreedomReads” or “Freedom Read”.
First names only. No last name anywhere, on screen or in captions.
No ID badge, lanyard card or DOC number is readable in any frame. Zoom to 200% on every shot to check.
“ILP” is always capitals. “Inside Literary Prize” is written in full the first time it appears.
Say “incarcerated people” in any text. Never “inmates”.
No Minnesota files: no WSP000xx without “v”, no P1055350/354/378.
Captions are low, long lines split in two, and gone before the end card.
Lips match the audio across every trim.
Book titles are exact: Martyr! (with “!”), My Friends, The Book Censor's Library, All Fours. Author names spelled right.
No book card or caption says which book won the prize.

transcript:
Auto-transcript of 20260611WSPv00047.MOV (Brandon, ILP 2026 judge, Washington State Penitentiary, 11 Jun 2026). Times are mm:ss in the source file. Speaker labels are automatic and sometimes wrong. “A9” is the transcript's spelling of the book Ædnan.
[00:02] So, what did you think about A9?
[00:05] I thought that A9 was a very visually appealing book and it painted a picture.
[00:11] I liked the way the book was formatted in a stanza form very similar to poetry which
[00:15] I have a natural desire for.
[00:17] And I do think that it gave a lot of insight on colonization and how it affects certain
[00:23] people.
[00:24] And what did you think about My Friends?
[00:28] I thought the book My Friends was a great story of coming together, of dealing with
[00:35] things and more importantly leaning on your village to handle trauma.
[00:38] Alright, and what did you think about the Book Censors Library?
[00:42] I thought the Book Censors Library was in motion on a page.
[00:46] It gave a wonderful story about family and about prioritizing what is important over
[00:52] what you want and more importantly knowing what things to put in front of you and how
[00:58] to keep those things in front of you in the best way possible.
[01:01] And what did you think about Martyr?
[01:03] I thought that Martyr was a wonderful illustration of self-discovery and perseverance in the
[01:09] face of trauma and adversity which we all face in our daily lives.
[01:13] Alright, and what did you think about All Fours?
[01:18] I thought that All Fours was a book that shed a lot of light on the perspective of women
[01:25] in our society and it definitely deserves the recognition of creating a higher appreciation
[01:32] for what our fellow women go through in our modern society.
[01:38] So what has reading these five books shown you that might surprise someone who thinks
[01:44] that books don't matter?
[01:46] There's a lot of relatability when it comes to reading and I truly think that reading
[01:52] these books you will find a small piece of yourself in every single one of the books.
[01:57] The real key is opening yourself up to the possibility of learning a little bit more
[02:01] about yourself.
[02:02] Something you may have already known and something you probably didn't think you did know.
[02:06] Alright, thank you.
[02:10] We out!
